title: Bombay Potatoes
subtitle: Spiced boiled potatoes fried with mustard seeds and turmeric
excerpt: Boiled potatoes fried in oil with mustard seeds, turmeric, and cumin until the outside is crisp and the spices have coated every piece. Works as a side dish or a light meal with flatbread.
sourceNotes: Anglo-Indian spiced potato dish as it appears on British curry-house menus, derived from Indian aloo masala traditions.

recipe.batchNotes: Boil a large batch of potatoes and fry to order in smaller portions as needed.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Boil the potatoes up to a day ahead and refrigerate. Cold potatoes fry more crisply.

content.text: Bombay potatoes work because the potatoes are boiled until just tender before they meet the oil, so the frying step is about building a spiced crust rather than cooking them through. The most common mistake is adding them to a pan that is not hot enough, which makes them steam instead of fry.
Boil the potato chunks in well-salted water for 10 to 12 minutes until just tender when pierced with a knife. Drain and leave to steam dry for 5 minutes.
Heat the oil in the frying pan over a high heat. Add the mustard seeds and cumin seeds and let them pop for 20 seconds. Add the curry leaves if using.
Turn the heat to medium. Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes until softened. Add the garlic, ginger, and green chilli and stir for 1 minute.
Add the turmeric, coriander, cumin, and chilli powder. Stir for 30 seconds. Add the chopped tomatoes and cook for 4 minutes until they break down.
Turn the heat to high. Add the drained potatoes and toss well to coat in the spiced tomato base.
Cook for 5 minutes, pressing the potatoes gently against the pan and turning them every minute, until the edges are crisp and golden.
Season with salt. Scatter with coriander and serve hot.

items.symptom: The potatoes are mushy and falling apart.
items.cause: They were boiled for too long before frying.
items.fix: Pull the potatoes out when a knife just pierces them; they will continue cooking in the pan. Cold leftover potatoes work even better.

items.symptom: The spices are not sticking to the potatoes.
items.cause: The tomatoes left too much moisture in the pan.
items.fix: Cook the tomato base until it is thick and most of the water has gone before adding the potatoes.

items.symptom: The potatoes are not getting crisp.
items.cause: The pan is not hot enough or is overcrowded.
items.fix: Use a wide pan, cook in a single layer, and resist moving them for a full minute at a time so a crust forms.
